_comment: Starting values for the waste transport planner UI. Companion to waste_rules.json, which holds what the trucks and chicos are physically allowed to carry (fixed), and to no_go_zones.json, which holds the areas some of them may not drive through; this one holds what the planner may change from day to day. Everything but the solver block and the chico costs is editable in the planner's Config tab; edits live in the browser only, so change this file to move the defaults. The solver block has no UI at all and is only set here. Times are local HH:MM, durations are minutes. Read by frontend/public/waste_model.js through frontend/server.js (/defaults.js).

company._comment: company site: trucks start and end the day here. Must be inside the routing area loaded by OSRM (Portugal).

fleet._comment: trucks of each type available on a normal day; keys are the truck types of waste_rules.json

chicos._comment: chico attachments available on a normal day; keys are the chico types of waste_rules.json. count: how many the company has (never more are offered than trucks of the matching type). What taking one costs the plan is part of the cost model, under costs.by_vehicle["chico:<key>"].

container_stock._comment: empty containers of each size the company has in the yard for a normal day; keys are the sizes of waste_rules.json. Only operations that take a container out of the company use them up: delivering an empty one, the empty half of an exchange, and materials (which leave in a container of that size). Picking up a full container at a client does not, it brings one in. When more operations than containers need a size, the extra ones are left unassigned and the solver decides which, the same way it decides everything else (priority first, then what the plan costs). Leave a size out, or set it to null, for a stock large enough not to matter. Editable in the planner's Config tab.

working_day._comment: lunch is spent at the company: every truck is back and unloaded by lunch_start and loads nothing before lunch_end, so the day is a morning and an afternoon shift, both planned in one solve; equal start and end mean no lunch. early_start_max_min is how much earlier than start a truck may go out, per truck type of waste_rules.json (a plain number instead of the block means the same for every type). It is offered in two steps, half of it and all of it, on the morning shift only, since the afternoon begins when lunch ends: the day is extended at the front, the end does not move, and the solver decides which trucks come in early against what it costs (costs.early_start_per_hour, one price for the whole fleet). A type left out, or set to 0, is offered no early start at all and costs nothing in solving time; that is the behaviour before this existed. Every step is one more vehicle per truck of that type for the solver to weigh, so allow it where it is needed rather than everywhere.

costs._comment: What a plan costs the company, in money. The only thing that varies with the plan is what the trucks burn on the road, so the cost of a route is (chico multiplier) x (cost per km of the truck type) x km. Nothing else is priced: the drivers are on a monthly salary, so their time is spent whether a truck goes out or not, and pricing it would trade real fuel against money already gone. Time is still a hard limit through the working day of a truck, it just costs nothing. Editable in the planner's Costs tab; edits live in the browser only, so change this file to move the defaults.

per_km._comment: cost of one kilometre for each truck type of waste_rules.json: fuel, tyres, wear, everything that scales with the road. Only the differences between the types decide which truck drives; the absolute level is handled by the planner (see solverPerKm in frontend/public/waste_model.js). The values below are placeholders, all equal, which makes every type cost the same per km: replace them with the company's real figures.

chico_multiplier._comment: what attaching a chico does to that truck's cost per km, per chico type of waste_rules.json: 1.25 means a quarter dearer with the trailer on. 1 lets the solver take a chico whenever it saves kilometres, which is the behaviour before this had a value.

costs._comment_afternoon: what sending a truck out after lunch is worth avoiding. One price for the whole fleet, charged once per truck that works the afternoon however many operations it does there, so a truck already out does its next one for free. 0, the value here, is the right answer for most days and is the behaviour before this existed: with a morning and an afternoon of equal length the solver values them identically and the plan lands in the morning regardless, while the afternoon work such a plan does contain is work the morning could not hold, which no price can move since operations rank above cost. It is a lopsided day this is for — a short morning against a long afternoon, where the afternoon genuinely is the cheaper half and whole days end up in it. Measured on a 16-operation day with a 2h morning and a 6h afternoon, a price of 10 moved 30 of the 32 tasks back into the morning for 0.6 km more driving. It also decides the matter on an even day, where the two halves tie and the morning currently wins by the order the trucks happen to be offered in rather than by anything the model says. Unlike the early start this is not money the company spends — nobody is paid for the afternoon who is not paid for the morning — so it is left out of what a plan is reported to cost; the Costs tab shows what a value is worth in kilometres of the dearest truck, which is the honest way to pick one. It needs a lunch to mean anything: without one the day is a single shift with no afternoon to charge, and the planner warns about it.
costs._comment_early_start: what one hour of early start costs, for a truck going out before the working day begins (working_day.early_start_max_min). Unlike a driver's ordinary time this is a real cost — it is worked on top of the day, not inside it — so it is priced and traded against the kilometres it saves: a truck comes in early when doing so saves more road than the early hours cost. It cannot keep an operation from being done, though: the solver does the most operations first and only then looks at money. Priced at 0 the early start is free, which makes trucks go out early for no reason, so the planner warns about it.

limits._comment: Hard caps per truck and shift, not costs: a route breaking one of them is not a plan at all, whereas a cost only makes it less attractive. 0 means no limit. With a lunch, each cap applies to the morning and to the afternoon separately, not to the whole day. max_tasks counts VROOM tasks, i.e. shipment steps, not planner operations: an exchange is four of them (two pickups and two deliveries). Editable in the Costs tab.

scenarios._comment: What the day is solved for, one plan per entry, offered side by side in the planner so the choice between them is the planner's. The solver minimises the money a route costs on the road plus a charge on its driving time, and time_weight is the only thing that changes between the entries: it multiplies that charge, so 1 is money with time merely breaking ties (the plan this planner gave before scenarios existed) and higher values buy less driving with money. Roughly, for a truck averaging 30-40 km/h: a few percent of the cost is time at 1, about half of it in the tens, nearly all of it in the hundreds. On a generated 20-operation day with the fleet and prices below, weight 1 came to 505 km and 9h42 of driving for EUR 348 over 7 trucks, weight 30 to 397 km and 7h49 for EUR 406 over 5, and weight 300 to 355 km and 7h03 for EUR 485 over 2 — road and hours fall together and money rises against both, because what the weight really decides is the size of truck: the cheap small ones carry little and so make many more trips. Note that the driving is added up over the whole fleet, so less of it buys truck-hours rather than a day that ends earlier. Everything else — the fleet, the operations, the prices, the limits, the working day — is identical across the entries, which is what makes the plans comparable. Each one is a full solve, so the day takes as long to plan as there are entries here (about half a second each on that 20-operation day); cut the list to two, or to one, to get that time back. key must be unique, label names the row in the planner's table and hint is the line under it.
scenarios.label: Mais barato
scenarios.hint: O que o dia custa à empresa: os quilómetros ao preço do camião que os faz. Os camiões pequenos são baratos mas levam pouco, por isso esta é também a opção com mais estrada.

scenarios.label: Equilibrado
scenarios.hint: Uma hora ao volante pesa aproximadamente o mesmo que os quilómetros que percorre. Meio-termo: menos estrada do que o dia mais barato, menos dinheiro do que o mais curto.

scenarios.label: Menos condução
scenarios.hint: O menor número de horas na estrada, e com elas os menos quilómetros: camiões maiores, menos viagens, mais dinheiro. É a condução somada em toda a frota, não a hora a que o último camião chega.

solver._comment: geometry, exploration_level and threads are in the planner's Costs tab; show_request has no UI and is only set here. geometry: ask the solver for the driven route (vroom's -g) so the map follows the roads and distances are reported, off draws straight lines between stops. exploration_level: vroom's -x, 0 (fastest) to 5 (best); vroom-conf/config.yml holds the server's own default and this overrides it per request. threads: vroom's -t. show_request: append the JSON sent to the solver under the summary, for debugging.
